   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Mark Longhorn, BRISTOL

Dear Ron and Brian,

Another query! I've noticed a
rather strange problem with my
SAM and I wondered if someone
could tell me the cause. If I
use the machine for over half an
hour, then switch off and then
switch it on again to use soon
after, the video signal is so
distorted that I cannot use the
machine.

I think this has something to do
with the fact that the power
supply and the video signal come
from the same box, and something
is overheating. If this is the
case, is there some heatsinking
I can do?

If I switch the machine on from
'cold', there is no problem
whatsoever and I never get
signal distortion during a
session.

Hope someone can help!

       Yours sincerely,

         Mark Longhorn

Brian Cavers to Mark Longhorn

You do not say if you have tried
retuning the television when the
video from the SAM is distorted.
Televisions from a few years ago
generally have an AFC (automatic
frequency control) which can
compensate for signals that
drift off the wavelength like
the SAM. Television transmission
nowadays does not drift and so
newer televisions no longer use
AFC but stick rigidly to the set
wavelength.

If this is the problem with your
set up there are three possible
things you might try...

1. Retune the channel whenever
   it drifts off the wavelength.

2. Retune a different channel to
   be in tune if your SAM drifts
   off slightly so you then can
   quickly switch channel and
   yet switch back again as you
   need to.

3. Buy an older, second-hand tv
   with an AFC button (some have
   a manual button; some have a
   concealed button that is
   depressed when you push down
   a flap to conceal the tuning
   switches).

If retuning has no effect you
might try opening up your PSU
unit and carefully turn one of
the screws to tune it to another
wavelength and then retune your
tv to that wavelength. It may or
may not cure the problem.

TAKE GREAT CARE - THERE IS A
TRANSFORMER IN THE UNIT AT MAINS
VOLTAGE. I DO NOT ACCEPT ANY
RESPONSIBILITY IF ANYONE SHOCKS
OR HARMS THEMSELVES!

There are two or three adjuster
screws. I recommend you stick
with one at a time, note its
starting position, turn it only
a few times - noting how many -
and turn it back if no success
before trying another screw. One
or two of the screws are fragile
ceramic and can easily break!

Failing that,if you're convinced
it is the PSU unit then new ones
can be bought from GREENWELD(see
LOOKOUT) or you might ring Bruce
Gordon for advice on 0792 797770
as he does repairs.    - Brian

From: John Plant, CANNOCK

Dear Chezron,

The "STYLE WRITER" is brilliant.
For the first time I am able to
use my Coupe as a word processor
for Church minutes etc. Congrat-
ulations to Darren Talbot.

Can the clip-art screens from
OUTLET be incorporated in STYLE
WRITER graphics? (For SAM). I'll
send for them anyway [OUTLET
EXTRA 2 - "CLIPPER":`3.50 - Ed]
and see what I can do. If the
worst comes to the worst (as
they say) I will have to print
out the graphics and fit the
writing in around them. Keep up
the good work.
                    - John Plant

Brian Cavers to John Plant

Yes - but they need to be first
converted into Mode 4 screens...

1.Load FLASH.

2.Select Mode 1 at the Mode Menu

3.Load the clip art screen.

4.If the screen is a pink blank
  then select SPEC'M COLOURS in
  the SCREEN Menu.

5.Select Mode 4 to convert.

6.Colour in image if wanted with
  the FILL option.

7.Save the screen.
                    more...

8.Boot the STYLEWRITER Menu and
  select IMAGER and follow the
  prompts to load the screen and
  create and save an image file.

9.Load STYLEWRITER and then load
  the image file(see SW manual).
  Once loaded, you can then
  insert any number of copies of
  the image anywhere in the text
  file at the cursor position.It
  will show as a grey patterned
  block on-screen but when you
  print it, the original image
  will be printed. Remember to
  make sure you have GRAPHICS ON
  at the print menu.

                         - Brian

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Ron and Brian,

Thank you for the Mk11 version
of OUTWRITE! I was pleased with
the first version but the second
was far beyond what I expected.
I'd think there are not many
readers suggestions that have
not been included or catered for
in one way or another. Congratu-
lations to all concerned.

Having said that there is always
one that has to be awkward.I use
rollpaper a lot so don't need to
bother about perforations, page
length or form feeds to either
skip perforations or go to the
top of the page - but I do often
need to do two or more copies.

I found neither of the options
on answering "continuous?" is
really ideal with "continuous "
sending a FORM FEED after each
print, wasting a lot of paper at
times and printing by pages is a
bit of a pest.I couldn't find an
option or user set-up to remove
this. So,for anyone interested,
this FF was tracked down and for
my purposes has been changed to
an LF. Memory location 75044 has
the BYTE value 12 for a FF (for
the LC10)so I found the simplest
way was to exit to user BASIC,
POKE 75044,10(for LF)and restart
with GOTO 1. A permanent change
can be made by reSAVing the cus-
tomised version or alternatively
if needed to be changed often,
written in the user BASIC area.

It is worth mentioning that on
(my) LC10 the manual says the
FORM FEED CHR27, 12 is inoperat-
ive if friction paper is used.
In fact it gives a one-line
reverse feed. The single code 12
does give a FF on friction
setting.

The option menu "send FF" is
carried out in BASIC line 34592
so deleting the CHR27 suited my
roll paper use.

I will now use the SPELLCHECKER
and reform to 32 chars per line
which will give the boys at
Leicester a bit of extra time to
have a second cup of tea. [We
don't have time for a first one
usually! -Ed]

     OUTWRITE! SPELLCHECKER

A reader mentioned the problem
of being quick off the mark to
sometimes stop with the correct
highlighted word and so being
able to enter using "E".

A very simple way is to add a
PAUSE at the end of line 472.
The list is put up as normal but
if a highlighted word is dis-
played the list stops and waits
for a prompt. SPACE returns to
menu and any other key continues
the search.

As a reminder a screen prompt
can be given and the following
is an example.


472 IF FAV THEN LET POSS$ = M$:
    CALL &0151: PRINT #0;AT 0,9;
    "SPACE to stop search"; AT
    0,34;" ANY KEY to continue":
   PAUSE : PRINT #0; AT 0,34;" "

An alternative is to use PAUSE X
and make X a value to give a
delay after a highlighted word
to give time to press space. The
prompt is not then needed.
There is also a possibility of
going one better. The line 472
is as above and added to the
prompt is "E to enter". Now, in
addition to "continue search"
and "exit to menu" at the last
highlighted word entering "E"
will put this word into the text
file and continue the search so
cutting out the menu option
stage.

To do this alter line 473,

473 IF INKEY$ = " " THEN GOTO
    479: ELSE IF INKEY$ = "E" OR
    INKEY$="e" THEN LET I$= "E":
    GOTO 479

Now alter line 391...

391 IF I$= "E" THEN GOTO 393 :
    ELSE IF LEN...as original...


For anyone thinking of adding a
"likely list" as was originally
suggested in line 472 if the
word is not highlighted then FAV
=0, FAV=1 if it is and the
current word in M$ is put into
POSS$ where POSS$ holds the last
highlighted word.

Thank you for printing my query
asking about software options on
a printer buffer. I have in the
meantime been able to obtain the
instruction book so all has been
revealed. Out of interest they
are as follows:
1) AUTO-PS. You were close with
"auto printer switch" it is in
fact "AUTO PAUSE", decides if
the printer is put on "PAUSE" or
"ON LINE" when first powered up
or after a reset. (Is this
really a "software" option?)

2) ACAD-CAL. This is as
suspected; it relates to being
used with IBM PC running autoCAD
software and driving a Calcomp
plotter. This mode recognises
the serial protocol used by
these systems.

3) SOFT-CON. (Another one I
found after posting off the
query) confirms my second
thought that the buffer can be
controlled from software. Using
command ESC, 0h, X. the buffer
can be remotely controlled to
carry out a number of functions
such as CLEAR, multiple copies,
switch inputs and outputs
between serial and parallel etc.

The advantages of the higher
capacity of 1M really shows its
advantages with colour dumps
from SAM. 1/2 hour for the
printer to do the dump but only
3 min for all data to be
processed and sent to the buffer
with the computer then free
while the printer slogs on.

The serial/parallel (in either
direction) conversion built in
means the Spectrum RS232 will
work with a Centronics printer
and it is also possible to have
both serial and Centronics
printers. Probably old hat but I
found with the application of a
file on a 6-pin telephone plug,
it fits the Spectrum RS232
socket a treat.

         Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

I used telex rolls myself years
ago. The firm I worked for threw
out partly-used ones because it
was crucial they did not run out
overnight. If you use the normal
continuous option, although it
"wastes" paper, at least the end
result is much neater if you cut
up the roll paper all the same
page lengths instead of one 9"
long and the next one 6" long!
Still,you seem to have found the
ideal solution for your needs.

A pause in the spell suggester
is a good idea and I may include
it in the master copy and add
the FF poke to the README file
perhaps!
                        - Brian

From: Daniel Cannon, NOTTS.

This is basically an appeal to
West Coast Computers. I've
written direct to them as well,
but this is to make the appeal
more public. See if you agree
with what I'm saying: I'd like
to see a new SAM made. One which
is compatible with the current
one and all its add-ons but one
which has some new features.

If you've seen any Amiga/PC/
console games you will have not-
iced most games have scrolling
and sound. There are a few
without scrolling (Ugh/Pushover/
Pang are some of the latest) but
the design of the game is
extremely good to get around
this.

All games have sound - but in
varying degrees of quality. With
SAM it's just 'above' Spectrum
128K/Amstrad CPC type music- not
too good really.

People  blame SAM's graphics and
sound chip because of this. The
fact is they are not to blame.
The resolution and colours of
the graphics are quite adequate
(but obviously it would be nice
to have these improved as well),
and if you've heard any decent
PD sample demo you'll know that
SAM is on a par with the likes
of an Amiga.

The problem is how they are
used. The other computers that
I've mentioned (apart from the


Speccy and Amstrad of course)
have extra hardware on board to
access the memory directly
(DMA). This hardware can copy
bytes around the memory and send
bytes to the sound chip far more
quickly that the processor ever
can. Put simply, the hardware
can play samples, print sprites,
or scroll the screen whilst the
processor gets on with other
work - so it isn't bogged down
with doing this stuff itself.
Result: Fast scrolling games
with lots of sprites on screen
and decent sampled music.

But even utility programs can
benefit - wordprocessors, data-
bases, and so on could use it to
copy information around the
memory faster.

Art packages would work faster
(especially the 'cut & paste'
option in FLASH). And at last
there will be a proper sample
sequencer program (like SOUND
MACHINE or ETracker but with
samples, not waveforms).

I know that people who own SAMs
know that their computer is good
for programming, experimenting
with, and so on, and they were
probably part-way attracted to
SAM because of that but most of
the people buying home computers
choose their computers because
of the quality and also quantity
of the games available. To make
SAM mass-market (or as mass-
market as it will ever get to be
now) we need better games - and
lots of them.

Basically, SAM needs a blitter
chip, and a DMA sample player.
Preferably in an interface box
which can be easily plugged in
the back so that older SAM
owners can upgrade. There are a
few other things I'd like to
see but these are the main two.
I'm sure with the amount of
talent around in the SAM world
that it can be done - it just
needs someone with the ability
to get things co-ordinated (and
the cash, of course).

Unfortunately, I know next to
nothing about building hardware,
but I can tell anybody who does
know what I'd like (and I'm sure
other programmers can tell the
designer(s) what they'd like
too).

Obviously, if nobody wants this
kit then it won't be built. That
is why I've written to as many
fanzines/user groups as I can
find to see how people react. If
enough people want this kit (and
let's face it - you'd be mad not
to want it)then it will probably
be built. Please write in to say
how you feel about the subject -
and put forward any ideas which
you may have yourself.

        Daniel  Cannon,
        programmer, ZAT Software


From: P. Ellis, STROUD



Dear Ron,

Ref:OUTWRITE!I am a little rusty
over the PRINTER set up. I have
a SHINWA CP 80. Can you help in
any way?

Thanks for your recent letter,
it's nice to have friends.

       Yours sincerely,

             Percy

Brian Cavers to Percy Ellis


It is not clear what the problem
is. I can only guess at four
possibles:


1.You don't know how to connect
  your printer to your SAM.

2.You do no know how to print
  anything from OUTWRITE.

3.You do not know how to insert
  printer codes in the text.

4.You don't know how to redefine
  printer codes for the CP 80.
  (or don't know what the codes
  are).

1. The SAM does not come with a
printer port: you need to buy a
printer interface. Contact FRED
PUBLISHING (see last month's
LOOKOUT). I'm pretty sure they
have the printer interfaces on
their list.

2. To print from OUTWRITE you
simply press EDIT twice to get
Menu 2 and press P to print.

3. To insert printer codes in
the text press EDIT once for
Menu 1, press X and then the
character that represents the
code, e.g., I for italics. They
are listed in the manual.

4. To change the printer codes,
alter the driver (see OUTWRITE
manual and your CP-80 manual).

If still no luck, write again
with more details of exactly
what you have and have not been
able to do. Is your printer
connected?Are you able to LPRINT
simple text in BASIC? Can you
dump screens with DUMP? Can you
print normal text from OUTWRITE?
Does the SHINWA CP-80 have a
Centronics parallel port or an
RS232 serial port? Is it Epson-
compatible? Is it working O.K.
separately from OUTWRITE?

The more information you can
give me the more chance I will
have of being able to help so
spell out every detail that may
be relevant.

                        - Brian

From: Glen Cook, Glenco Software

Dear Brian,

Thank you for sending me a copy
of the comparative review of
SCADs and Games Master. [In last
month's OUTLET - Ed.]
I would like to take this oppor-
tunity to clarify the situation
with regards to copyright and
using SCADs.

It is very difficult to know how
far to take the copyright restr-
ictions with utility software
like SCADs. When I started to
write the package,I was inform-
ed by ENIGMA VARIATIONS that
there was a huge piracy problem
with SAM based software(in fact,


I believe ENIGMA pulled out of
the SAM market because of this
problem). At the time of writing
the manual, we did not intend to
make the Designer copy protected
and so we printed the copyright
message within the manual stat-
ing that the 'SUPERVISOR' could
not be distributed with any
software written using SCADs.


We have invested a huge amount
of money into the SCADs package,
and obviously we want to see a
return from our investment, we
believed, at the time of writing
the manual, that limiting the
distribution of the 'SUPERVISOR'
would protect our investment.


Since completing the manual, we
decided to take a different
approach, and so we make the
'DESIGNER'program(key disc) copy
protected. You will notice that
the'SUPERVISOR'is not protected
in this way.Since the 'DESIGNER'
is needed to create new games,
we now feel that copies of the
'SUPERVISOR' CAN be distributed
with programs written using
SCADs. However, the 'DESIGNER'
is still covered by our copy-
right and protection system.


Please feel free to publish any
demonstrations you create or
receive along with the SCADs
Supervisor.


I would like to take this oppor-
tunity to make one or two comm-
ents on the review. You seem to
make a great deal about the fact
that Games Master is supplied
with a compiler and that SCADs
is not. If you wrote two ident-
ical programs using each system,
you will find that the BASIC
version of the SCADs game and
the compiled version of Games
Master game actually run at
about the same speed.

You make no mention anywhere
within the review about the room
designer,this is a major feature
within SCADs and something which
is sadly lacking within Games
Master. It would be extremely
difficult to write a large flip


screen game using Games Master
because of the lack of room
within the program modules.

The flip screen is the most
popular game format, after
scrolling games. Games Master
programmers would find it
extremely difficult,for example.
to write a game of similar qual-
ity to the demo game supplies on
the SCADs disc (demo1) simply
because Games Master will not
allow for a large number of
rooms. The demo's supplied with
Games Master bear this out, they
all consist single screens.

I don't want to be critical of
Andy's work, as what he has
achieved in the time it took to
.

develop the program is good. The
two systems have been designed
for two game formats. Games
Master is excellent for creating
games with single screens,
whereas SCADs is designed to
create big flip screen games.

Surely the manual does not have
spelling mistakes, I thought
they were grammatical errors?
'Grammatical errors', in my
opinion, sound so much better
than 'spelling mistakes'. I
believe that in the long term,
the benefit of SCADs will tip
the scales in its favour.

Enough of this moaning, please
find enclosed a copy of the
compiled version of Demo1.[It
should be in ADD-ENDERS - Ed]

As I mentioned earlier in this
letter SCADs BASIC runs at
around the same speed as Andy's
compiled BASIC. This is an
example of the speed that a
compiled game will run. It is a
great deal faster than Andy's
compiled BASIC.

I know that you are going to
moan, when the compiler is re-
leased, that the customer is
going to have to fork out x
number of pounds for a separate
compiler, when Games Master
alreade includes a compiler. The
fact of the matter is, the SCADs
compiler is a true compiler.
There will be a large number of
BASIC commands covered by the
compiler and there will be very
few restrictions.

The actual code produced by the
compiler will be a great deal
more efficient and faster than
the code produced by Andy's
compiler.

Our initial test show that games
written using the compiler
will run, on average, 4 times
faster than the equivalent BASIC
games. This means that the
games will run 4 times faster
than Andy's compiled games. [See
demo in Add-Enders compared to
last month's version - Ed.]

The compiler will be supplied
with another comprehensive man-
ual, with, hopefully no gram-
matical errors. The compiler
will be supplied with a full


screen text editor, which will
enable the creation and editing
of programs so much simpler. The
screen editor is very similar to
a word processor, very fast.

The compiler will not use SAM
BASIC as such, instead it will
feature a RISC BASIC instruction
set, with labels as opposed to
line numbers. Once the compiler
is released, both packages will
merge to create the ultimate 8
bit games designing system. You
will not be able to tell the
difference bewtween games
written using the SCAD system
and professionally created
games.

Please note our new address...


Glenco Software, 1 Osborne Rd.,
Oxbridge, STOCKTON ON TEES
Cleveland TS18 4DJ

        Yours sincerely,

           Glen Cook

Brian Cavers to Glen Cook

I agree with most of what you
say and will just pick up one or
two points...

I don't think I was thinking of
speed in my reference to the
fact that GAMES MASTER produces
compiled code but rather that it
a single neat block of code that
could be immediately offered for
sale whereas originally SCADS
games had the copyright limit. I
couldn't personally care what
goes on "behind the scenes" in a
program (at least in that sense)
- it's the result that matters
and if SCADS BASIC runs as fast
as GAMES MASTER compiled code
then I certainly would not
complain about the method used.

I think it is misleading to say
GAMES MASTER can only produce
single-screen games. It might be
that SCADS can add more screens
(I can't tell) but I would be
amazed if there is any extreme
restriction on GAMES MASTER in
that respect. I cannot conceive
of any commercial game with only
one or two screens!

I did not have time to explore
the room designer in SCADS and I
could not do justice to either
package in the time available to
me. I accept it is a major
feature as it certainly looks
most comprehensive.

Whether spelling or grammar, any
errors in the manual were very
minor.It is just that the manual

is so professionally and beauti-
fully produced that even small
errors glared at me from the
pages! It is worth adding that
the explanations in the manual
are exceptionally clear and easy
to follow -giving the underlying
principles as well as the actual
applications.

I'm not sure that it is fair to
infer that the GAMES MASTER
compiler is not a true compiler
and the forthcoming SCADS one is
because,like most compilers,they
compile a reduced instruction
BASIC into code. You may well be
right about the extra efficiency
and speed of the SCADS compiler
though! I shall try not to moan
at the extra price -but you have
to compete in the market! -Brian

From: Mark Longhorn, BRISTOL

Dear Ron and Brian,

Another query! I've noticed a rather strange problem with my SAM and I wondered if someone could tell me the cause. If I use the machine for over half an hour, then switch off and then switch it on again to use soon after, the video signal is so distorted that I cannot use the machine.

I think this has something to do with the fact that the power supply and the video signal come from the same box, and something is overheating. If this is the case, is there some heatsinking I can do?

If I switch the machine on from 'cold', there is no problem whatsoever and I never get signal distortion during a session.

Hope someone can help!

Yours sincerely,

Mark Longhorn

Brian Cavers to Mark Longhorn

You do not say if you have tried retuning the television when the video from the SAM is distorted. Televisions from a few years ago generally have an AFC (automatic frequency control) which can compensate for signals that drift off the wavelength like the SAM. Television transmission nowadays does not drift and so newer televisions no longer use AFC but stick rigidly to the set wavelength.

If this is the problem with your set up there are three possible things you might try...

1. Retune the channel whenever it drifts off the wavelength.

2. Retune a different channel to be in tune if your SAM drifts off slightly so you then can quickly switch channel and yet switch back again as you need to.

3. Buy an older, second-hand tv with an AFC button (some have a manual button; some have a concealed button that is depressed when you push down a flap to conceal the tuning switches).

If retuning has no effect you might try opening up your PSU unit and carefully turn one of the screws to tune it to another wavelength and then retune your tv to that wavelength. It may or may not cure the problem.

A reader mentioned the problem of being quick off the mark to sometimes stop with the correct highlighted word and so being able to enter using "E".

A very simple way is to add a PAUSE at the end of line 472. The list is put up as normal but if a highlighted word is dis- played the list stops and waits for a prompt. SPACE returns to menu and any other key continues the search.

As a reminder a screen prompt can be given and the following is an example.

472 IF FAV THEN LET POSS$ = M$: CALL &0151: PRINT #0;AT 0,9; "SPACE to stop search"; AT 0,34;" ANY KEY to continue": PAUSE : PRINT #0; AT 0,34;" "

An alternative is to use PAUSE X and make X a value to give a delay after a highlighted word to give time to press space. The prompt is not then needed. There is also a possibility of going one better. The line 472 is as above and added to the prompt is "E to enter". Now, in addition to "continue search" and "exit to menu" at the last highlighted word entering "E" will put this word into the text file and continue the search so cutting out the menu option stage.

To do this alter line 473,

473 IF INKEY$ = " " THEN GOTO 479: ELSE IF INKEY$ = "E" OR INKEY$="e" THEN LET I$= "E": GOTO 479

Now alter line 391...

391 IF I$= "E" THEN GOTO 393 : ELSE IF LEN...as original...

From: Daniel Cannon, NOTTS.

This is basically an appeal to West Coast Computers. I've written direct to them as well, but this is to make the appeal more public. See if you agree with what I'm saying: I'd like to see a new SAM made. One which is compatible with the current one and all its add-ons but one which has some new features.

If you've seen any Amiga/PC/ console games you will have not- iced most games have scrolling and sound. There are a few without scrolling (Ugh/Pushover/ Pang are some of the latest) but the design of the game is extremely good to get around this.

All games have sound - but in varying degrees of quality. With SAM it's just 'above' Spectrum 128K/Amstrad CPC type music- not too good really.

People  blame SAM's graphics and sound chip because of this. The fact is they are not to blame. The resolution and colours of the graphics are quite adequate (but obviously it would be nice to have these improved as well), and if you've heard any decent PD sample demo you'll know that SAM is on a par with the likes of an Amiga.

The problem is how they are used. The other computers that I've mentioned (apart from the

Speccy and Amstrad of course) have extra hardware on board to access the memory directly (DMA). This hardware can copy bytes around the memory and send bytes to the sound chip far more quickly that the processor ever can. Put simply, the hardware can play samples, print sprites, or scroll the screen whilst the processor gets on with other work - so it isn't bogged down with doing this stuff itself. Result: Fast scrolling games with lots of sprites on screen and decent sampled music.

But even utility programs can benefit - wordprocessors, data- bases, and so on could use it to copy information around the memory faster.

Art packages would work faster (especially the 'cut & paste' option in FLASH). And at last there will be a proper sample sequencer program (like SOUND MACHINE or ETracker but with samples, not waveforms).

I know that people who own SAMs know that their computer is good for programming, experimenting with, and so on, and they were probably part-way attracted to SAM because of that but most of the people buying home computers choose their computers because of the quality and also quantity of the games available. To make SAM mass-market (or as mass- market as it will ever get to be now) we need better games - and lots of them.

Basically, SAM needs a blitter chip, and a DMA sample player. Preferably in an interface box which can be easily plugged in the back so that older SAM owners can upgrade. There are a few other things I'd like to see but these are the main two. I'm sure with the amount of talent around in the SAM world that it can be done - it just needs someone with the ability to get things co-ordinated (and the cash, of course).

Unfortunately, I know next to nothing about building hardware, but I can tell anybody who does know what I'd like (and I'm sure other programmers can tell the designer(s) what they'd like too).

Obviously, if nobody wants this kit then it won't be built. That is why I've written to as many fanzines/user groups as I can find to see how people react. If enough people want this kit (and let's face it - you'd be mad not to want it)then it will probably be built. Please write in to say how you feel about the subject - and put forward any ideas which you may have yourself.

Daniel  Cannon, programmer, ZAT Software

### OUTWRITE! SPELLCHECKER

Один читатель упоминал проблему: порой трудно среагировать вовремя, чтобы остановиться на нужном подсвеченном слове и ввести его нажатием "E".

Очень простой способ — добавить команду PAUSE в конец строки 472. Список выводится как обычно, но если отображается подсвеченное слово, вывод останавливается и ждет нажатия клавиши. ПРОБЕЛ возвращает в меню, а любая другая клавиша продолжает поиск.

В качестве напоминания можно вывести подсказку на экран, вот пример:

```text
472 IF FAV THEN LET POSS$ = M$:
    CALL &0151: PRINT #0;AT 0,9;
    "SPACE to stop search"; AT
    0,34;" ANY KEY to continue":
    PAUSE : PRINT #0; AT 0,34;" "
```

Другой вариант — использовать `PAUSE X`, где X — задержка после подсвеченного слова, чтобы успеть нажать пробел. Подсказка в этом случае не нужна.

Но можно сделать еще лучше. Строка 472 остается как выше, а к подсказке добавляется "E to enter". Теперь, помимо «продолжить поиск» и «выйти в меню», при нажатии "E" на последнем подсвеченном слове это слово будет вставлено в текстовый файл, и поиск продолжится, минуя этап вызова меню.

Для этого измените строку 473:

```text
473 IF INKEY$ = " " THEN GOTO
    479: ELSE IF INKEY$ = "E" OR
    INKEY$="e" THEN LET I$= "E":
    GOTO 479
```

Теперь измените строку 391...

```text
391 IF I$= "E" THEN GOTO 393 :
    ELSE IF LEN...как в оригинале...
```

Для тех, кто думает добавить «список вероятных слов», как изначально предлагалось: в строке 472, если слово не подсвечено, то `FAV=0`, а если подсвечено, то `FAV=1`, и текущее слово из M$ помещается в POSS$, где POSS$ хранит последнее подсвеченное слово.

Спасибо, что опубликовали мой вопрос о программных опциях буфера принтера. Тем временем мне удалось достать руководство по эксплуатации, так что все прояснилось. Если кому интересно, вот они:

1) AUTO-PS. Вы были близки с "auto printer switch" (автопереключатель принтера) — на самом деле это "AUTO PAUSE", определяющий, переводится ли принтер в режим "PAUSE" или "ON LINE" при включении питания или после сброса. (Действительно ли это «программная» опция?)

2) ACAD-CAL. Тут все, как и предполагалось: режим предназначен для работы с IBM PC под управлением AutoCAD и управления плоттером Calcomp. Этот режим распознает последовательный протокол, используемый этими системами.

Если вы видели какие-либо игры для Amiga/PC/консолей, вы наверняка заметили, что в большинстве игр есть скроллинг и звук. Есть несколько проектов без скроллинга (Ugh/Pushover/Pang — одни из последних), но дизайн этих игр невероятно хорош, что и компенсирует его отсутствие.

Во всех играх есть звук — но разного качества. На SAM это просто уровень «чуть выше» музыки в стиле Spectrum 128K/Amstrad CPC — на самом деле не слишком здорово.

Люди винят в этом графику и звуковой чип SAM. На самом же деле они вовсе не виноваты. Разрешение и цвета графики вполне адекватны (хотя, разумеется, было бы здорово улучшить и их), и если вы слышали хоть одно приличное PD-сэмпл-демо, вы знаете, что SAM вполне наравне с той же Amiga.

Проблема в том, как всё это используется. Другие компьютеры, о которых я упомянул (за исключением, конечно же, Speccy и Amstrad), имеют на борту дополнительное «железо» для прямого доступа к памяти (DMA). Это оборудование может копировать байты в памяти и посылать байты в звуковой чип намного быстрее, чем когда-либо сможет процессор. Проще говоря, аппаратура может проигрывать сэмплы, выводить спрайты или скроллить экран, пока процессор занят другой работой — так что он не перегружен выполнением этой рутины. Результат: игры с быстрым скроллингом, кучей спрайтов на экране и приличной сэмплированной музыкой.

Но даже утилиты могут извлечь из этого выгоду — текстовые процессоры, базы данных и тому подобное могли бы использовать это для более быстрого копирования данных в памяти.

Графические редакторы работали бы быстрее (особенно опция «cut & paste» в FLASH). И, наконец, появится нормальная программа сэмплерного секвенсора (вроде SOUND MACHINE или ETracker, но с сэмплами, а не волновыми формами).

Я знаю: владельцы SAM в курсе, что их компьютер хорош для программирования, экспериментов и так далее, и отчасти именно поэтому SAM их и привлек. Но большинство людей, покупающих домашние компьютеры, выбирают их из-за качества и количества доступных игр. Чтобы сделать SAM продуктом массового рынка (насколько это сейчас вообще возможно), нам нужны более качественные игры — и в больших количествах.

По сути, SAM нужен чип-блиттер и DMA-плеер сэмплов. Желательно во внешнем корпусе интерфейса, который легко подключается сзади, чтобы владельцы более старых SAM могли проапгрейдиться.
